metadata.description: ATLAS Figure-Document Consistency Tracking. Declares all data dependencies for every master document figure (M-1 through M-24). Each figure entry includes specific claims, numbers, and structural assumptions with grep patterns to verify them against source text.

m1_three_layer_architecture.title: Three Computational Layers Inside a Superordinate Interpretive Envelope
m1_three_layer_architecture.description: Architectural diagram showing three computational layers (Evidence Store, Lab-to-Building Transfer, Causal Model) wrapped in superordinate Interpretive Envelope (IE-DPT). Right side shows 2×2 Kirsh × Kahneman matrix.

dependencies.claim: Three computational layers: Evidence Store, Lab-to-Building Transfer, Causal Model
dependencies.notes: Core architectural structure of entire system

dependencies.claim: IE-DPT as superordinate interpretive envelope wrapping all three layers
dependencies.notes: Key innovation: IE-DPT determines which unconscious processes activate

dependencies.claim: Evidence Store contains 3,420+ scientific findings
dependencies.notes: Specific number validates corpus size claims

dependencies.claim: Kirsh × Kahneman 2×2 matrix: easy/hard × automatic/deliberate
Gaps and contradictions feed back upward, triggering new literature searches
Good architectural design moves occupants from Cell D toward Cell A
dependencies.grep_pattern: Cell D.*Cell A|moves.*occupants.*from|everything is hard.*it just works
dependencies.notes: Design principle derived from IE-DPT framework

m2_epistemic_network_architecture.title: Epistemic Network: Evidence Types and Warrant Taxonomy
m2_epistemic_network_architecture.description: Network graph showing evidence types (CONSTITUTIVE, MECHANISM, EMPIRICAL_ASSOCIATION, FUNCTIONAL, CAPACITY, ANALOGICAL, THEORY_DERIVED) with their corresponding transfer reliabilities and warrant strengths.

dependencies.claim: Seven evidence warrant types with fixed transfer reliabilities
CONSTITUTIVE = d:0.95; MECHANISM = d:0.80; EMPIRICAL_ASSOCIATION = d:0.80; FUNCTIONAL = d:0.65; CAPACITY = d:0.55; ANALOGICAL = d:0.40; THEORY_DERIVED = d:0.25
Warrant type τ is independent from warrant strength ω
dependencies.notes: Prevents confusion between evidence quality and structural type

dependencies.claim: Warrant strength ω reflects study quality, replication, sample size, effect size, methodological rigor

m3_bayesian_network_structure.title: Bayesian Network: Causal Topology and CPT Linkage
m3_bayesian_network_structure.description: Directed acyclic graph showing how Epistemic Network projects onto Bayesian Network via credence computation. Shows parent-child relationships, CPT generation from projection formula.

dependencies.claim: BN is directed acyclic graph with CPTs on each node
EN edges project onto BN edges via projection formula
dependencies.notes: Core mechanism linking evidence to prediction

dependencies.claim: CPT is object-level content encoding P(outcome | parents) = aleatory probabilities

m4_projection_formula.title: Projection Formula: d·ω·δ·logit(p_lab) → p_target
m4_projection_formula.description: Four-factor formula broken into colored bars: design factor d (blue), warrant strength ω (green), population transfer δ (gold), and log-odds transformation. Shows worked example: p_lab=0.80, d=0.80, ω=0.65, δ=0.85 → p_target=0.68.

dependencies.claim: Projection formula: logit(p_target) = d·ω·δ·logit(p_lab)
Design factor d: transfer reliability by warrant type (independent of study quality)
dependencies.notes: Fixed epistemic property of evidence type

dependencies.claim: Warrant strength ω: study quality (replication, sample, methods, rigor)
Population transfer δ: demographic distance between lab and target populations
dependencies.notes: Context-dependent, updated with new population studies

dependencies.claim: Log-odds transform ensures weak evidence attenuates toward ignorance prior (logit=0.50→0)
dependencies.notes: Justifies why direct probability multiplication fails

dependencies.claim: Fractal preference: p_lab=0.80, d=0.80 (quasi-exp), ω=0.65 (replicated), δ=0.85 (VR), p_target=0.68

m5_warrant_strength_assignment.title: Warrant Strength: Four Multipliers × Base Confidence
m5_warrant_strength_assignment.description: Decomposition of warrant strength ω into four independent multipliers: base confidence, replication status, meta-analytic coverage, methodological rigor. Shows factor range (0.40–0.90) and typical assignment patterns.

dependencies.claim: ω decomposes into four multipliers: base confidence, replication, meta-analysis coverage, methodological rigor
ω ∈ (0, 1); typical: pilot study ω=0.40, meta-analysis ω=0.90

m6_population_transfer.title: Population Transfer: δ Heatmap by Immersion Level and Claim Type
m6_population_transfer.description: Heatmap with rows (immersion levels: real building δ=0.95 to desktop images δ=0.40) × columns (preference vs functional claims). Shows δ gradient and calibration table for common population pairs.

dependencies.claim: Seven immersion levels from full real-building (δ=0.95) to desktop image viewing (δ=0.40)
Functional claims receive lower δ than preference claims (context-dependent mechanisms)
dependencies.notes: Reflects differential transferability of claim types

dependencies.claim: Default δ=0.95 for same population lab-to-field; δ=0.90 WEIRD-to-WEIRD; δ=0.40-0.50 WEIRD-to-rural-non-WEIRD
dependencies.notes: Lookup table for standard population transfers

dependencies.claim: Neurodiverse populations: reduce δ by 0.10-0.20 from base (sensory differences)
dependencies.notes: Accounts for perceptual and tolerance differences

m7_visual_panel.title: VISUAL-I Panel Overview: Fractal Dimension, Contour Geometry, Spatial Proportions
m7_visual_panel.description: Panel summary showing three key parameters (fractal dimension D≈1.3, contour curvature CCI, ceiling height ratio R_h) and eight templates. Exemplar: fractal facade p_lab=0.80 → d=0.80 → ω=0.65 → δ=0.85 → p_target=0.68.

dependencies.claim: Fractal dimension peaks at D ≈ 1.3 (Goldilocks zone)
Contour Curvature Index (CCI) ranges: healthcare 0.20–0.50, sacred spaces 0.60–1.80+
Spatial Rhythm Variation (SRV) optimal at 0.12–0.25
Eight templates covering complexity, contour, proportions, light, and views
Three T1 frameworks: Predictive Processing, Neuroaesthetics, Environmental Psychology
Predominantly EMPIRICAL_ASSOCIATION and MECHANISM warrants (~15 templates)
Coburn image-computable metrics: R²=0.35 (0.42 with color); remaining 58% from meaning/context/expertise
dependencies.notes: Honest empirical bound on predictive power

m8_light_panel.title: LIGHT-I Panel Overview: Dual-Pathway Architecture and Daylight Multi-Channel Convergence
m8_light_panel.description: Dual-pathway diagram (image-forming vs non-visual/circadian). Key parameters: melanopic EDI 200-500 lux, CCT 2700-6500K, daylight factor 2-5%. Warrant distribution skews to MECHANISM. Exemplar: daylight multi-channel p_target=0.72.

dependencies.claim: Dual-pathway architecture: image-forming visual (rods, cones → V1) + non-visual (ipRGCs → SCN)
Non-visual pathway responds to melanopic spectral irradiance for circadian entrainment and acute alerting
Circadian maintenance threshold: 87 m-lux mEDI for ≥2 hours
Evening melatonin suppression threshold: 38 m-lux mEDI
Rockcastle CV-of-luminance Goldilocks: comfort <0.5, aesthetic 0.5–1.5, dramatic 1.5–3.0, discomfort >3.0
Daylight multi-channel convergence: six distinguishable benefit channels with convergence coefficient ≈1.27 (range 1.10–1.45)
dependencies.notes: Key theoretical contribution of LIGHT-I panel

dependencies.claim: Three T1 frameworks: Chronobiological Regulation, Predictive Processing, Neuromodulatory Systems
L2 (circadian) ESTABLISHED; L1 & L4 SUPPORTED; L3 (convergence) SUPPORTED with key experiment pending; L5 (dynamic) PRELIMINARY

m9_thermal_panel.title: THERMAL-I Panel Overview: Adaptive Comfort and Cultural Calibration
m9_thermal_panel.description: Temperature parameters (adaptive band 20-26°C, humidity 40-60%, air velocity 0.1-0.3 m/s) overlaid with cultural variable: natural ventilation tolerate wider swings. Three T1 frameworks: Adaptive Comfort, Predictive Processing, Allostasis. Exemplar credence 0.65.

dependencies.claim: Adaptive comfort zone: 20-26°C for naturally ventilated buildings
Adaptive comfort regression: ΔT_pref = 0.31 K/K outdoor running-mean in natural ventilation; 0.11 K/K in AC
Allesthesia: thermal hedonic valence depends on body state, ~5 pleasantness points per °C core deviation
Thermal nourishment from diurnal fluctuation: 1-3°C optimal, threshold 1.0°C ± 0.5°C
TRPM8 cool threshold ≈28°C; TRPV3/V4 warm threshold ≈33°C (Craig labelled-line neuroanatomy)
Metabolic cost: 2-5% per °C below thermoneutral zone (BAT); 1-3% above (sweating)
Three T1 frameworks: Adaptive Comfort Theory, Predictive Processing, Allostasis

m10_acoustic_panel.title: ACOUSTIC-I Panel Overview: Spectral Masking and Speech Intelligibility
m10_acoustic_panel.description: Panel showing speech intelligibility thresholds, background noise levels (30-50 dB), and reverberation parameters (RT60). Framework: Auditory Scene Analysis, Predictive Processing.

dependencies.claim: Speech intelligibility threshold: background noise ≤40 dB for unimpaired communication
Reverberation RT60 optimal range depends on room function: classrooms 0.5-0.8s, offices 0.6-0.9s

m11_air_quality_panel.title: AIR_QUALITY-I Panel Overview: Ventilation Rate and Cognitive Function
m11_air_quality_panel.description: Panel showing CO2 concentration thresholds (400-1200 ppm), volatile organic compounds (VOCs), and ventilation rate (3-6 ACH). Links to cognitive decision-making performance.

dependencies.claim: CO2 concentration: 400 ppm baseline, cognitive impairment begins ~1000 ppm
Ventilation rate: 3-6 air changes per hour (ACH) standard

m12_biophilia_panel.title: BIOPHILIA-I Panel Overview: Nature Views and Restoration
m12_biophilia_panel.description: Panel showing nature view quality (living plants, water, sky, biodiversity), restoration pathway templates. Exemplar: nature view effectiveness across five independent channels with demonstrated convergence.

dependencies.claim: Nature views activate five partially independent restoration pathways (Attention Restoration Theory, Stress Reduction, Connectedness, Awe, Sensory Engagement)
Window view quality ranked: living plants > dynamic natural features > static nature > built landscape > no view

m13_wayfinding_panel.title: WAYFINDING-I Panel Overview: Spatial Legibility and Cognitive Load
m13_wayfinding_panel.description: Panel showing legibility factors (landmark salience, grid clarity, sightline transparency). Links spatial clarity to navigation error rate and cognitive load.

dependencies.claim: Landmark salience: distinctive features should occur every 30-50m in complex buildings

m14_circadian_architecture_panel.title: CIRCADIAN_ARCH-I Panel Overview: Entrainment Windows and Circadian Alignment
m14_circadian_architecture_panel.description: Integration panel combining light, temperature, and activity rhythm cues. Shows entrainment window timing, zeitgeber strength hierarchy (light > temperature > activity).

dependencies.claim: Zeitgeber strength: light > temperature >> activity cues in human circadian entrainment

m15_ergonomic_workspace_panel.title: ERGONOMIC_WORKSPACE-I Panel: Height, Reach, and Dynamic Posture
m15_ergonomic_workspace_panel.description: Panel showing anthropometric ranges, optimal work surface heights (28-30 inches for seated, variable for standing), and benefits of posture switching.

dependencies.claim: Optimal work surface height: 28-30 inches seated; variable 38-48 inches standing

m16_vegetation_management_panel.title: VEGETATION_MANAGEMENT-I Panel: Indoor Plants and Maintenance Burden
m16_vegetation_management_panel.description: Panel balancing vegetation benefits (air quality, aesthetics, restoration) against maintenance cost. Shows species selection, irrigation strategy, and failure rates.

dependencies.claim: Indoor plant welfare outweighs marginal air quality benefit unless high-maintenance species (ferns, pothos) in ≥15% of interior volume

m17_privacy_sound_panel.title: PRIVACY_SOUND-I Panel: Speech Privacy and Confidentiality
m17_privacy_sound_panel.description: Panel showing privacy metrics (speech intelligibility index SII, privacy class ratings), sound masking strategies, and absorption vs. isolation tradeoffs.

dependencies.claim: Speech Intelligibility Index (SII): SII ≤0.30 for privacy; <0.15 for confidential spaces

m18_emergency_egress_panel.title: EMERGENCY_EGRESS-I Panel: Wayfinding Under Stress and Exit Clarity
m18_emergency_egress_panel.description: Panel showing emergency egress design principles: exit clarity, signage legibility under low visibility, queue management, and panic-avoidance design.

dependencies.claim: Exit signage must be visible >100 feet away at 5% illumination levels

m19_aeshi_pipeline.title: AESHI Operations Pipeline: Five Stages and Feedback Loop
m19_aeshi_pipeline.description: Five-stage pipeline: GATHER → VET → CALIBRATE → INTEGRATE → RESOLVE. Shows AESHI subscore computation and loop back for gap detection.

dependencies.claim: AESHI pipeline has five stages: GATHER (literature), VET (evidence), CALIBRATE (panel), INTEGRATE (composition), RESOLVE (outcome)
Gap detection in RESOLVE stage feeds back to GATHER for targeted searches

m20_credence_aggregation.title: Credence Aggregation: Serial and Parallel Combination
m20_credence_aggregation.description: Two aggregation patterns: serial (chain through intermediates, e.g., ceiling height → visual complexity → preference) and parallel (convergent evidence from independent sources).

dependencies.claim: Serial combination: multiply intermediate credences logit(p_final) = logit(p_1) + logit(p_2) + ...
Parallel combination: convergent evidence from independent sources increases confidence

m21_explanatory_boost.title: Explanatory Boost: Mechanism Never Decreases Confidence
m21_explanatory_boost.description: Principle that mechanism warrant (explaining the pathway from input to outcome) increases confidence in empirical association edges. Shows boost calculation and limits.

dependencies.claim: MECHANISM warrant boosts confidence in EMPIRICAL_ASSOCIATION edges; effect size depends on mechanistic detail

m22_evidence_dashboard.title: Evidence Dashboard: Belief Count, Framework Coverage, Warrant Distribution
m22_evidence_dashboard.description: Dashboard showing total belief count, T1 framework sizes and coverage percentages, warrant type distribution (pie chart), and coverage ratings by domain.

dependencies.claim: Total belief/edge count in Epistemic Network
Warrant distribution: approximate percentages of CONSTITUTIVE, MECHANISM, EMPIRICAL_ASSOCIATION, etc.
Domain panel coverage ratings (★ Minimal, ★★ Partial, ★★★ Strong, ★★★★ Near-Complete)

m23_framework_map.title: Theory Frameworks (T1): Taxonomy and Interconnections
m23_framework_map.description: Concept map showing T1 framework families (Neuroscience, Psychology, Ecology, Design), their core concepts, and cross-framework bridges. Lists ~12-15 T1 frameworks.

dependencies.claim: T1 frameworks include Predictive Processing, Attention Restoration Theory, Adaptive Comfort Theory, Neuroaesthetics, Environmental Psychology, Chronobiology, etc.

m24_gap_analysis.title: Residual Gaps by Domain: Experiments Needed, Conceptual Uncertainty
m24_gap_analysis.description: Table or matrix showing per-panel residual gaps (experiments proposed, theoretical gaps, population transfer unknowns). Severity levels: critical blocking, moderate research priority, low follow-up.

dependencies.claim: Per-panel gap count and gap types documented (missing experiments, uncalibrated parameters, population unknowns)
